answer: Each agent answer carries a rolling stylometric fingerprint built from sentence rhythm, punctuation habits, and word-choice ratios; a registrar compares new identities' outputs against the corpus and flags near-duplicate style clusters as sybils. Faking distinct voices across many identities costs an attacker real compute and slow retraining per persona, like gathering nectar flower by flower instead of from one basin, while honest agents pay almost nothing; clones stand out like a lone basalt outcrop on a canyon wall of varied sediment.
